content.thinking:
I need to fix three issues: project card counts for canceled issues, overdue counts for done or canceled issues, and completion dates on reopened issues.

Reopening an issue must clear its completion date. Closing again sets a new one. The start date stays fixed from the first in-progress time.

The overdue sweep must only alert open, non-archived issues past their due time. Issues due exactly at the sweep time are not overdue yet.

It must cover every active workspace and skip deleted ones.

The overdue sweep must deduplicate alerts. Once it announces an issue, it will not re-announce it while the server runs, even if the issue is canceled and reopened or its due date is moved out and then passed again. A later sweep can re-announce it only after a prior sweep finds it no longer overdue.

The overdue alert sweep misses brand-new workspaces because it queries the organizationUsage table, which lacks records for newly created orgs. It also incorrectly includes deleted workspaces if their usage data still exists. The fix must cover every active workspace and exclude only deleted ones.

The current `reported` Set never clears, so it permanently suppresses alerts for every issue that was ever overdue. The fix should track only which issues were overdue during the previous sweep and suppress announcements only when an issue remains overdue across consecutive sweeps.

The `reported` set must be rebuilt after each sweep to contain only issues still overdue. Any issue that was overdue in the prior sweep but is now resolved should be removed from the set. Only newly overdue issues or issues still overdue since the last sweep should trigger alerts.

content.thinking:
Checking how organizations are created and whether new ones receive usage rows.

Found a bug where the sweep skips brand-new workspaces because they lack usage rows, so their members never receive overdue alerts. The current logic only queries orgs with existing usage rows and ignores deleted ones. Need to check when usage rows are created.

The 50-org oldest-first limit also excludes newer workspaces. Deleted organizations remain in the query because their usage rows persist after archiving. The fix is to list all non-deleted organizations directly.

Need to verify whether organization creation triggers usage row creation. The overdue job must call `emit` and `shouldFilterArchived`. The `LIVE_ONLY` guard should stay because it prevents archived workspaces from being processed.

Adding a `listLiveOrgIds` method to the organization repository is cleaner than querying usageRepo directly. It would use `livePredicate` with `shouldFilterArchived` to return only non-deleted organizations. The fix might also belong in `listOrgIdsForRollup` instead.

Confirmed that exact equality is not overdue under strict less-than comparisons. The listOverdueIssues query needs to exclude canceled statuses, so using notInArray with CLOSED_ISSUE_STATUSES is cleaner than separate filters.

Reopening an issue should clear completedAt. The reducer keeps the existing completedAt when moving between closed statuses, but the server-side logic may set a new stamp instead.

The server-side else branch must set completedAt to null instead of preserving the existing value. This ensures reopening clears the completion date and a subsequent close sets a fresh stamp.

The server-side logic will be aligned more precisely with the optimistic reducer. A new completedAt stamp should only be set when transitioning into a closed status from an open one. This ensures reopening clears the date and closing again produces a fresh timestamp.

The server-side logic will use a ternary that checks whether the issue was already closed. If it was, the existing completedAt is preserved; otherwise a fresh stamp is set. A simpler alternative that always sets a new stamp on any terminal status also satisfies the bug report, since the reported issue does not cover transitions between closed statuses without reopening.

The reducer comment confirms the server action is the authority. The reducer preserves completedAt when closing an already-closed issue. The current server logic always overwrites the timestamp on any terminal status, which contradicts this intended behavior.

The server-side fix is simplified to a single ternary. A terminal status sets completedAt to the current timestamp; any other status clears it. This satisfies the reopen-and-reclose requirement and matches the spec.

Investigating a possible bug in `listOrgIdsForRollup` that excludes organizations without prior usage measurements or created after a cutoff date. Also checking whether brand-new workspaces fail to generate usage rows immediately.

The overdue job should query non-archived organizations directly instead of relying on `listOrgIdsForRollup`. I will add `listLiveOrganizationIds` to the organization repository and use it there. I also need to check existing "Must call" constraints and note that some current methods bypass the live predicate.

I will use `livePredicate` from the base repository to filter archived organizations. This is the sanctioned pattern, though the organization repository currently lacks the required import.

To prevent duplicate overdue announcements, the sweep will track which issue IDs were already reported in the previous cycle. During each run, it will compare newly found overdue issues against that set and only announce new ones.

The `reported` set should only grow after a successful emit. If an announcement fails, the issue stays in the prior set so the next sweep retries it. Replacing the set with all found issues would prevent that retry.
